name: Bergen County
intro: Bergen County is New Jersey's most populous county, a patchwork of roughly 70 suburban boroughs and townships directly across the Hudson River from Manhattan, with Hackensack as its county seat. Much of its housing stock dates from the pre-war and early postwar decades, and commuting runs heavily toward New York City via the George Washington Bridge and NJ Transit's Pascack Valley, Main and Bergen County lines.
permitNotes: Home improvement contractors must hold a statewide HIC registration from the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs. Building permits are issued locally by each municipality's construction office under the NJ Uniform Construction Code.

name: Essex County
intro: Essex County pairs Newark, New Jersey's largest city and the county seat, with dense inner-ring cities like East Orange and Irvington and leafier suburbs such as Bloomfield and West Orange to the west. Housing ranges from Newark's rowhouses and pre-war multifamilies to early-20th-century single-family neighborhoods, and NJ Transit's Morris & Essex lines and Newark Penn Station anchor commuting into New York.
permitNotes: Home improvement contractors must hold a statewide HIC registration from the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs. Building permits are issued locally by each municipality's construction office under the NJ Uniform Construction Code.

name: Middlesex County
intro: Middlesex County sits at the center of the state along the NJ Turnpike and Northeast Corridor rail line, with New Brunswick, home of Rutgers University, as its county seat. It is dominated by large postwar townships like Edison, Woodbridge and Old Bridge alongside older industrial cities such as Perth Amboy, and it draws commuters to both New York and the Route 1 corridor's office and pharma employers.
permitNotes: Home improvement contractors must hold a statewide HIC registration from the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs. Building permits are issued locally by each municipality's construction office under the NJ Uniform Construction Code.

name: Hudson County
intro: Hudson County is the densest county in New Jersey, packed onto the Hudson River waterfront opposite Manhattan with Jersey City as its county seat. Rowhouse and tenement-era housing dominates older neighborhoods while high-rises line the Gold Coast waterfront, and the PATH system, ferries and the Hudson-Bergen Light Rail carry heavy daily commuting into New York.
permitNotes: Home improvement contractors must hold a statewide HIC registration from the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs. Building permits are issued locally by each municipality's construction office under the NJ Uniform Construction Code.

name: Monmouth County
intro: Monmouth County covers the northern Jersey Shore and its inland suburbs, with the county seat in Freehold Borough. Large postwar townships like Middletown, Howell and Marlboro sit alongside historic shore towns, and NJ Transit's North Jersey Coast Line plus ferry service from the Bayshore carry commuters to New York.
permitNotes: Home improvement contractors must hold a statewide HIC registration from the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs. Building permits are issued locally by each municipality's construction office under the NJ Uniform Construction Code.

name: Ocean County
intro: Ocean County stretches along the central Jersey Shore behind its barrier islands, with Toms River as the county seat and Lakewood as one of the fastest-growing municipalities in the state. Its housing stock is heavily postwar, including large planned retirement communities inland, and the Garden State Parkway is the county's main commuting spine.
permitNotes: Home improvement contractors must hold a statewide HIC registration from the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs. Building permits are issued locally by each municipality's construction office under the NJ Uniform Construction Code.

name: Union County
intro: Union County runs from the dense industrial cities of Elizabeth, its county seat, and Linden near Newark Bay to comfortable commuter suburbs like Westfield in the west. Housing spans pre-war two-families in the east to early-20th-century single-family neighborhoods along NJ Transit's Raritan Valley Line and Northeast Corridor.
permitNotes: Home improvement contractors must hold a statewide HIC registration from the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs. Building permits are issued locally by each municipality's construction office under the NJ Uniform Construction Code.

name: Morris County
intro: Morris County is an affluent, wooded county in north-central New Jersey with Morristown, a Revolutionary War headquarters town, as its county seat. Large townships like Parsippany-Troy Hills host corporate campuses along I-80 and I-287, and NJ Transit's Morris & Essex and Montclair-Boonton lines link its commuter towns to New York.
permitNotes: Home improvement contractors must hold a statewide HIC registration from the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs. Building permits are issued locally by each municipality's construction office under the NJ Uniform Construction Code.

name: Montgomery County
intro: Montgomery County is the most populous of Philadelphia's Pennsylvania suburbs, running from Main Line communities like Lower Merion through the King of Prussia commercial hub to Norristown, its county seat. Housing ranges from grand pre-war Main Line homes to postwar subdivisions, and several SEPTA Regional Rail lines feed Center City Philadelphia.
permitNotes: Home improvement contractors register statewide under HICPA with the Pennsylvania Attorney General's office. Building permits are issued at the municipal level, with each township or borough administering the PA Uniform Construction Code.

name: Bucks County
intro: Bucks County stretches from dense postwar Lower Bucks suburbs like Bensalem and the Levittown communities up through historic Doylestown, the county seat, to rural Upper Bucks along the Delaware River. Commuters use I-95, the Pennsylvania Turnpike and SEPTA's West Trenton and Lansdale/Doylestown Regional Rail lines.
permitNotes: Home improvement contractors register statewide under HICPA with the Pennsylvania Attorney General's office. Building permits are issued at the municipal level, with each township or borough administering the PA Uniform Construction Code.

name: Delaware County
intro: Delaware County contains some of Philadelphia's oldest and densest suburbs, from rowhouse-lined Upper Darby on the city border to Main Line communities like Radnor, with Media as the county seat. Much of its housing predates World War II, and SEPTA trolleys, the Market-Frankford El terminus at 69th Street and the Media/Wawa Regional Rail line serve its commuters.
permitNotes: Home improvement contractors register statewide under HICPA with the Pennsylvania Attorney General's office. Building permits are issued at the municipal level, with each township or borough administering the PA Uniform Construction Code.

name: Chester County
intro: Chester County is the fastest-suburbanizing of Philadelphia's collar counties, anchored by the borough of West Chester, its county seat, and growth corridors along Routes 202 and 30 through Tredyffrin, Exton and the western Main Line. Newer subdivisions mix with historic boroughs and preserved horse-country farmland, and SEPTA's Paoli/Thorndale line follows the old Main Line through the county.
permitNotes: Home improvement contractors register statewide under HICPA with the Pennsylvania Attorney General's office. Building permits are issued at the municipal level, with each township or borough administering the PA Uniform Construction Code.

name: Philadelphia County
intro: Philadelphia County is coterminous with the City of Philadelphia, the sixth-largest city in the United States and the anchor of the Delaware Valley region. Its housing stock is dominated by rowhouses spanning the 18th through 20th centuries, and SEPTA's subway, trolley, bus and Regional Rail network converges on Center City.
permitNotes: Home improvement contractors register under HICPA with the Pennsylvania Attorney General's office, and contractors working in the city also need licensing through Philadelphia's Department of Licenses and Inspections (L&I), which issues building permits citywide.

name: Kings County
intro: Kings County is coextensive with the borough of Brooklyn, the most populous of New York City's five boroughs. It spans dense brownstone neighborhoods, industrial waterfront districts, and residential areas from Greenpoint to Coney Island. Most residents commute within the city by subway and bus.
permitNotes: Home-improvement contractors in New York City are licensed by the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), and building permits are issued through the NYC Department of Buildings (DOB).

name: Queens County
intro: Queens County is coextensive with the borough of Queens, the largest of the five boroughs by land area and the second most populous. It is among the most ethnically diverse counties in the United States, with major hubs in Flushing, Jamaica, and Long Island City. Residents commute by subway, bus, and the Long Island Rail Road.
permitNotes: Home-improvement contractors in New York City are licensed by the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), and building permits are issued through the NYC Department of Buildings (DOB).

name: New York County
intro: New York County is coextensive with the borough of Manhattan, the commercial and cultural core of New York City. It is the destination for large daily commuter flows from the outer boroughs, Long Island, the Hudson Valley, and New Jersey. Housing stock is dominated by apartment buildings, from prewar walk-ups to high-rise towers.
permitNotes: Home-improvement contractors in New York City are licensed by the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), and building permits are issued through the NYC Department of Buildings (DOB).

name: Bronx County
intro: Bronx County is coextensive with the borough of the Bronx, the only NYC borough primarily on the U.S. mainland. It includes dense residential neighborhoods, Yankee Stadium, the Bronx Zoo, and large parks such as Van Cortlandt and Pelham Bay. Residents commute by subway, bus, and Metro-North.
permitNotes: Home-improvement contractors in New York City are licensed by the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), and building permits are issued through the NYC Department of Buildings (DOB).

name: Richmond County
intro: Richmond County is coextensive with the borough of Staten Island, the least populous of the five boroughs and the most suburban in character. It is connected to Brooklyn by the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge and to Manhattan by the Staten Island Ferry. Single-family and townhouse housing dominates much of the borough.
permitNotes: Home-improvement contractors in New York City are licensed by the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), and building permits are issued through the NYC Department of Buildings (DOB).

name: Nassau County
intro: Nassau County covers the western portion of Long Island immediately east of Queens, dominated by the large towns of Hempstead, North Hempstead, and Oyster Bay plus the cities of Glen Cove and Long Beach. It is a classic commuter county, with many residents riding the Long Island Rail Road into Manhattan. The county seat is Mineola.
permitNotes: Contractor licensing runs through the county consumer-affairs office, while building permits are issued by individual town, city, and village building departments. Licensed trades such as electricians and plumbers are often licensed at the town or county level on Long Island.

name: Suffolk County
intro: Suffolk County occupies the central and eastern portion of Long Island, from the Nassau border out to Montauk and Orient Point. Its largest towns are Brookhaven, Islip, Babylon, Huntington, and Smithtown, and the county seat is Riverhead. Western Suffolk is heavily commuter-oriented via the Long Island Rail Road, while the East End is known for farms, vineyards, and beach communities.
permitNotes: Contractor licensing runs through the county consumer-affairs office, while building permits are issued by individual town, city, and village building departments. Licensed trades such as electricians and plumbers are often licensed at the town or county level on Long Island.

name: Westchester County
intro: Westchester County lies immediately north of New York City in the lower Hudson Valley. Its largest municipalities are the cities of Yonkers, New Rochelle, Mount Vernon, and White Plains, the county seat, along with the large town of Greenburgh. Metro-North's Hudson, Harlem, and New Haven lines carry heavy commuter traffic into Grand Central Terminal.
permitNotes: Contractor licensing runs through the county consumer-protection office, while building permits are issued by individual town, city, and village building departments.

name: Rockland County
intro: Rockland County sits on the west bank of the Hudson River northwest of New York City, across the Mario M. Cuomo Bridge from Westchester. Its five towns are Ramapo, Clarkstown, Orangetown, Haverstraw, and Stony Point, with the county seat in New City. Commuters reach the city by bus, by NJ Transit rail lines, and via the bridge.
permitNotes: Contractor licensing runs through the county consumer-protection office, while building permits are issued by individual town, city, and village building departments.
